summary: Parity alone determines whether n or 2n is the least common multiple, so the accepted formula uses constant work and matches the unavoidable scalar output cost.

optimality.argument: A correct implementation must emit one integer and distinguish odd from even inputs, requiring Omega(1) work. One modulo test and at most one multiplication achieve O(1).

replacement_checks.evidence: Producing the integer result and distinguishing adjacent odd and even inputs requires Omega(1) work.
The accepted source performs one parity test and returns either n or 2n without iteration or input-sized storage.
Regression exhaustively checks all 150 legal inputs against an independent direct search through positive multiples.
